newsitem.title: USA: Six family members dead in West Virginia massacre.
newsitem.headline: Six family members dead in West Virginia massacre.

text.p: Police in Wheeling, West Virginia, Friday said they were investigating a late-night massacre in which a former mental patient shot and killed five relatives and then turned the gun on himself.
"It was the biggest set of homicides I've seen in 30 years," chief of detectives Lt. Clark Gable said. "He shot those children while they were sleeping ... I can't conceive how a father can do that."
Mark Storm, 30, of Wheeling apparently shot his wife Betty, 26, and daughters Megan, 3, and Jessica, 6, late on Thursday in their home using a 9-mm handgun, Gable said.

Storm then drove to his mother's home about 15 minutes away, Gable said. The bodies of his brother, Benjamin, 32, and his mother, Roberta Myles, 59, were found in the house. Myles was still alive but died later in a hospital.
Storm's body was found outside the house near a river with a gunshot wound to the head, Gable said. The gun was found nearby. Police do not yet have a motive for the killings.

Storm had left a mental facility at Ohio Valley Medical Centre in Wheeling earlier that day. In a prepared statement, the facility said he was a voluntary patient who had admitted himself on Sunday and was free to leave of his own accord.
It said he returned a short time later with his wife to get discharge instructions and make a follow-up appointment.
"We are deeply saddened and shocked by this tragedy," the statement said.
